1.q: מִ֚י כְּ⁠הֶ֣⁠חָכָ֔ם וּ⁠מִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ פֵּ֣שֶׁר דָּבָ֑ר
1.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one is like the wise person, because only a wise person knows the interpretation of a matter. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [No one is like the wise person, and no one else knows the interpretation of a matter!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **interpretation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what a matter means]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wisdom**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [That a person is wise]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if wisdom were a light that **enlightens** a person’s **face**. He means that wisdom gives a person a cheerful or gracious expression. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [gives him a cheerful expression]

Qoheleth is using **the strength of his face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “his harsh or stern expression.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and his harsh expression is changed] or [and it changes his harsh expression]

2.note: Here, **mouth** represents the king’s commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the commands of a king]

Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe an **oath** that involves **God**. This could mean: (1) an oath of loyalty to the king that a person made in the presence of God or (2) an oath that God made to support the king. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the oath that you swore before God]

3.note: Here, **face** represents the presence of the king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verse 12. Alternate translation: [Do not let fear of this king control you]

Qoheleth is using **Do not stand in a bad matter** as a common expression of the culture to mean “do not join in or continue with an evil plan.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not take part in an evil plan]

4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [And who will ask him what he is doing]

Qoheleth is imagining someone using the question form to challenge or rebuke the king for what he is doing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not do what you are doing!]

5.note: Qoheleth is using **will not know a bad matter** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will not experience harm.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will not experience any harm]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the **heart** of a wise person were the part of him that thinks and understands. He means the mind of a wise person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the mind of a wise person]

6.note: Qoheleth uses the word **because** here to indicate a contrast between the fact that there is a proper **time and procedure** for every matter and the fact that people suffer great **misfortune**. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [even though the misfortune of humanity is severe upon him]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **misfortune**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what troubles humanity]

Qoheleth is not referring to a specific person by **him**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [upon people]

7.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one can tell a person what will happen in the future. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [no one can declare it to him.]

8.note: Qoheleth is speaking of **wickedness** as if it were a living thing that could **deliver its masters**. He means that doing wicked things will not save wicked people from death. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and wicked people will not escape death by doing wicked things]

9.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:13. This also occurs in verse 16.

The expression **was done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [to every deed that people did]
See how you translated **under the sun** in 1:3. This also occurs in verses 15 and 17.

The pronoun **his** refers to a person who suffers **harm**. This could mean: (1) the person over whom someone else has authority. Alternate translation: [to the harm of the person he rules over] or (2) the person who has authority, who brings harm on himself by harming others. Alternate translation: [to his own harm, he brings harm to another] It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers.

10.note: The expression **buried** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people burying the bodies of wicked people]

The implication is that while these wicked people were alive, they regularly went into and out of **a place of holiness**, that is, the temple. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and while they were alive, they regularly entered and left the holy place, the temple]

The standard written Hebrew text as we have it today reads “And they were forgotten.” Other ancient manuscripts read “And they were praised.” The ULT follows that reading. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

The implication is that these **wicked people** had done evil deeds in the same **city** where people praised them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [where they had done these evil deeds]

The pronoun **This** refers to something that Qoheleth says is **vapor**. This could mean: (1) the situations that Qoheleth describes in the next two verses. Alternate translation: [What I am about to describe also is vapor] or (2) the situation that he has just described in this verse. Alternate translation: [People praising the wicked actions of others is also vapor] It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. This also occurs in verse 14.
See how you translated this same word in 1:2. This word also occurs in verse 14.

11.q: אֵין נַעֲשָׂ֣ה פִתְגָ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָ⁠רָעָ֖ה מְהֵרָ֑ה
11.note: The expression **is not made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those in authority do not quickly make a decree against the evil deed]

11.q: מָלֵ֞א לֵ֧ב בְּֽנֵי הָ⁠אָדָ֛ם בָּ⁠הֶ֖ם לַ⁠עֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע
11.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if **the heart** of people were a container that **fills** with the desire **to do evil**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people become fully determined to do evil]
See how you translated **the sons of humanity** in 1:13.

12.note: Qoheleth says **a hundred times** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means very many times. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [over and over again]

Qoheleth is using **lengthening days for himself** as a common expression of the culture to mean “living a long life.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and living a long life]

13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the shadow** soon passes away, so the life of a wicked person will come to an end. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [will he lengthen his days, which pass away quickly like a shadow]

14.note: The expression **is done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [vapor that happens on the earth]

The implication is that righteous people experience what **wicked people** deserve for their **deeds**, and wicked people experience what **righteous people** deserve for their **deeds**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [according to what the wicked people deserve for their deeds … according to what the righteous people deserve for their deeds]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:2.

15.note: Qoheleth is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **praised** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that this is his own conclusion. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [And I myself praised]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [people being joyful]

15.q: אֵֽין ט֤וֹב לָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַ⁠שֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּ֛י אִם לֶ⁠אֱכ֥וֹל וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁתּ֖וֹת וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׂמ֑וֹחַ
15.note: If it would appear in your language that Qoheleth was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [the only good thing for humanity under the sun is to eat and to drink and to rejoice]

Qoheleth is speaking of joy as if it were a living thing that could **accompany him in his toil**. He means that a person can experience joy while he works hard. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he will be able to experience joy in his toil]

16.q: אֶת הָ֣⁠עִנְיָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה עַל הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ
16.note: The expression **is done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the business that people do on the earth]

Qoheleth is referring to all of the time by naming two major components, **the day** and **the night**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [at all times]

Qoheleth is using **sleep in his eyes he is not seeing** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he does not sleep at all.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he is not sleeping at all]

The pronouns **his** and **he** refer to someone who does not sleep. This could mean: (1) any person who is busy with **the business that is done on the earth**. Alternate translation: [in his eyes a person who is busy with that business is not seeing] or (2) Qoheleth himself, who is speaking of himself in the third person. Alternate translation: [in my eyes, who am busy with that business, am not seeing]. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers.

17.q: לֹ֨א יוּכַ֜ל הָ⁠אָדָ֗ם לִ⁠מְצוֹא֙ אֶת הַֽ⁠מַּעֲשֶׂה֙
17.note: Qoheleth is using **find** as a common expression of the culture to mean “understand.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [humanity is not able to understand the deed]

17.q: בְּ֠⁠שֶׁ⁠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲמֹ֧ל הָ⁠אָדָ֛ם לְ⁠בַקֵּ֖שׁ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑א
17.note: Qoheleth uses the word **yet** here to indicate a contrast between how hard people work **to seek** and the fact that they **will not find**. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [on account of which, although humanity toils to seek, he will not find]
